segments.arabic: [1271] حدثنا حجاج بن منهال حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثني سليمان الشيباني قال: سمعت الشعبي قال: أخبرني من مر مع النبي ﷺ على قبر منبوذ
segments.english: Hajjaj ibn Minhal related to us: Shu‘bah related to us; he said: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to me; he said: I heard al-Sha‘bi say: One who passed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, by a grave set apart informed me:

segments.arabic: فأمهم وصلوا خلفه
segments.english: He led them, and they prayed behind him.

segments.arabic: قلت: من حدثك هذا يا أبا عمرو قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما
segments.english: I asked, “Who related this to you, Abu ‘Amr?” He said, “Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both.”

comparisons.note: Changes passing with the Prophet to a person who had seen him; renders praying behind him as forming rows. The earlier audit’s your Prophet description belongs to a different occurrence and is corrected here.

notes: The occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

Keep the full Sulayman al-Shaybani route, with the Prophet, led them and prayed behind him. The final question addresses Abu Amr and is a transmission exchange. The grave-set-apart reading is documented alongside the alternative foundling construction; no vocalization is silently supplied.

The historical opening transmission verb differs from selected and modern. Selected: «حدثني سليمان الشيباني». brill-1862 (PDF 335): «أخبرنا سليمان الشيباني». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 322): «حدثني سليمان الشيباني».

segments.arabic: [1272] حدثنا محمد بن الفضل حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن ثابت عن أبي رافع عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl related to us: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi‘, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him:

segments.arabic: أن أسود رجلا أو امرأة كان يقم المسجد فمات ولم يعلم النبي ﷺ بموته فذكره ذات يوم، فقال: ما فعل ذلك الإنسان قالوا مات يا رسول الله قال أفلا آذنتموني فقالوا إنه كان كذا وكذا
segments.english: A Black person—a man or a woman—used to sweep the mosque. The person died, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not know of his death. He mentioned him one day and asked, “What happened to that person?” They said, “He died, Messenger of Allah.” He said, “Why did you not inform me?” They said, “He was such and such”—

segments.arabic: قصته قال: فحقروا شأنه
segments.english: they mentioned his story. He said: They considered him of little importance.

segments.arabic: قال: فدلوني على قبره فأتى قبره فصلى عليه
segments.english: He said, “Then show me his grave.” He came to his grave and prayed over him.

comparisons.note: Absorbs the narrator’s story pointer and assessment into the reported reply. Keep the short story pointer and the separate narrator appraisal.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Huraira:

A black person, a male or a female used to clean the Mosque and then died. The Prophet (p.b.u.h) did not know about it . One day the Prophet remembered him and said, "What happened to that person?" The people replied, "O Allah's Apostle! He died." He said, "Why did you not inform me?" They said, "His story was so and so (i.e. regarded him as insignificant)." He said, "Show me his grave." He then went to his grave and offered the funeral prayer.
comparisons.note: Places فحقروا شأنه inside an explanatory parenthesis within reported speech, obscuring its narrator role.

notes: The occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

Keep the man-or-woman alternative and subsequent masculine pronouns. Al-Ayni explains قصته as an elliptical they mentioned his story; retain it and the separate narrator appraisal, outside the reported reply. Do not turn the narrator’s low-importance description into a Prophetic judgment.

segments.arabic: [1273] حدثنا عياش حدثنا عبد الأعلى حدثنا سعيد قال، وقال لي خليفة حدثنا ابن زريع حدثنا سعيد عن قتادة عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Ayyash related to us: ‘Abd al-A‘la related to us: Sa‘id related to us. He said: And Khalifah said to me: Ibn Zuray‘ related to us: Sa‘id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: العبد إذا وضع في قبره وتولي وذهب أصحابه حتى إنه ليسمع قرع نعالهم أتاه ملكان فأقعداه فيقولان له ما كنت تقول في هذا الرجل محمد ﷺ فيقول أشهد أنه عبد الله ورسوله فيقال انظر إلى مقعدك من النار أبدلك الله به مقعدا من الجنة
segments.english: “When the servant is placed in his grave and his companions have turned away and departed, he even hears the sound of their sandals. Two angels come to him and make him sit up. They ask him, ‘What did you use to say about this man, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ He says, ‘I testify that he is Allah’s servant and His Messenger.’ He is told, ‘Look at your place in the Fire. Allah has exchanged it for a place in the Garden.’”

segments.arabic: قال النبي ﷺ فيراهما جميعا وأما الكافر أو المنافق فيقول لا أدري كنت أقول ما يقول الناس فيقال لا دريت ولا تليت ثم يضرب بمطرقة من حديد ضربة بين أذنيه فيصيح صيحة يسمعها من يليه إلا الثقلين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “He sees them both. As for the disbeliever—or the hypocrite—he says, ‘I do not know. I used to say what the people said.’ He is told, ‘You neither knew nor followed.’ Then he is struck once between his ears with an iron hammer. He gives a cry that those near him hear, except humans and jinn.”

comparisons.note: Abridges the two opening transmission routes.

checkedBody: Narrated Anas:

The Prophet said, "When a human being is laid in his grave and his companions return and he even hears their foot steps, two angels come to him and make him sit and ask him: What did you use to say about this man, Muhammad ? He will say: I testify that he is Allah's slave and His Apostle. Then it will be said to him, 'Look at your place in the Hell-Fire. Allah has given you a place in Paradise instead of it.' " The Prophet added, "The dead person will see both his places. But a non-believer or a hypocrite will say to the angels, 'I do not know, but I used to say what the people used to say! It will be said to him, 'Neither did you know nor did you take the guidance (by reciting the Quran).' Then he will be hit with an iron hammer between his two ears, and he will cry and that cry will be heard by whatever approaches him except human beings and jinns."
comparisons.note: Abridges opening routes and adds a Quran-recitation explanation to ولا تليت; the final hearers’ relation is also rendered more narrowly.

notes: Preserve both opening routes, the narrator uncertainty and the two quoted responses without substituting English explanatory material.

Keep both opening routes, the unexpanded Ayyash and Ibn Zuray names, all three Prophetic honorifics and the disbeliever-or-hypocrite uncertainty. The working English uses the active companions turned away reading discussed by al-Ayni; Ibn Hajar and the modern vocalization also record a passive reading about attending to the deceased’s affairs. Do not silently vocalize the selected source. The following reading of تليت is one classical lexical analysis; Quran recitation and other explanations remain alternatives in the commentary, not extra quoted objects. Keep one iron hammer, one blow and near him.

The historical second route has a transfer marker and the name Yazid, absent from selected and modern. Selected: «وقال لي خليفة حدثنا ابن زريع». brill-1862 (PDF 335): «ح وقال لي خليفة حدثنا يزيد بن زريع». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 322): «وقال لي خليفة حدثنا ابن زريع».

The modern occurrence has إذ where selected and historical have إذا. Both remain recorded without a source alteration. Selected: «العبد إذا وضع». brill-1862 (PDF 335): «العبد إذا وضع». dar-ibn-kathir-2002 (PDF 322): «العبد إذ وضع».

segments.arabic: [1274] حدثنا محمود حدثنا عبد الرزاق أخبرنا معمر عن ابن طاوس عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Mahmud related to us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: أرسل ملك الموت إلى موسى عليهما السلام فلما جاءه صكه فرجع إلى ربه، فقال أرسلتني إلى عبد لا يريد الموت فرد الله عليه عينه، وقال ارجع فقل له يضع يده على متن ثور فله بكل ما غطت به يده بكل شعرة سنة قال أي رب ثم ماذا قال ثم الموت قال: فالآن فسأل الله أن يدنيه من الأرض المقدسة رمية بحجر
segments.english: The angel of death was sent to Musa, peace be upon them both. When he came to him, he struck him. He returned to his Lord and said, “You sent me to a servant who does not want death.” Allah restored his eye and said, “Return and tell him to place his hand on the back of an ox. For every hair his hand covers, he will have a year.” He said, “My Lord, then what?” He said, “Then death.” He said, “Then now.” He asked Allah to bring him near to the holy land, a stone’s throw away.

segments.arabic: قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: فلو كنت ثم لأريتكم قبره إلى جانب الطريق عند الكثيب الأحمر
segments.english: He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “If I were there, I would show you his grave beside the road, by the red sand dune.”

comparisons.note: Specifies a black eye beyond the selected صكه; a fuller injury clause exists in the historical print but is absent from this selected occurrence.

checkedBody: Narrated Abu Huraira:

The angel of death was sent to Moses and when he went to him, Moses slapped him severely, spoiling one of his eyes. The angel went back to his Lord, and said, "You sent me to a slave who does not want to die." Allah restored his eye and said, "Go back and tell him (i.e. Moses) to place his hand over the back of an ox, for he will be allowed to live for a number of years equal to the number of hairs coming under his hand." (So the angel came to him and told him the same). Then Moses asked, "O my Lord! What will be then?" He said, "Death will be then." He said, "(Let it be) now." He asked Allah that He bring him near the Sacred Land at a distance of a stone's throw. Allah's Apostle (p.b.u.h) said, "Were I there I would show you the grave of Moses by the way near the red sand hill."
comparisons.note: Supplies severe slapping/eye injury and explanatory action beyond the selected صكه. Keep the historical injury clause as a variant, and preserve the selected dual honorific scope.

notes: The historical print has an eye-injury clause absent from selected and modern text. English explanations must not silently insert it.

Keep the dual peace honorific for Musa and the angel, struck him without importing the historical eye-injury clause, restored his eye, each hair/year, then now, the stone’s-throw distance and the separate Messenger statement. Do not insert an angel-return scene or an explicit I want to die statement.

The historical print adds an eye-injury clause and uses a different honorific. The selected dual honorific and shorter wording remain unchanged. segments.arabic: [1275] حدثنا عثمان بن أبي شيبة حدثنا جرير عن الشيباني عن الشعبي عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: ‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us: Jarir related to us, from al-Shaybani, from al-Sha‘bi, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى النبي ﷺ على رجل بعد ما دفن بليلة قام هو وأصحابه وكان سأل عنه، فقال من هذا فقالوا فلان دفن البارحة فصلوا عليه
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed over a man one night after he had been buried. He and his companions stood. He had asked about him, saying, “Who is this?” They said, “So-and-so; he was buried last night.” Then they prayed over him.

comparisons.note: Its burial-at-night wording can lose the selected interval بعد ما دفن بليلة; review time relations directly from the Arabic.

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Abbas:

The Prophet (p.b.u.h) offered the funeral prayer of a man one night after he was buried, he and his companions stood up (for the Prayer). He had asked them about him before standing, saying, "Who is this?" They said, "He is so and so and was buried last night." So all of them offered the funeral prayer.
comparisons.note: Adds an explanatory standing relation beyond the selected report.

notes: The occurrence was located by its body and chain in both inspected prints and English passages. Wording, role and honorific review remain pending.

segments.arabic: [1276] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us; he said: Malik related to me, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: لما اشتكى النبي ﷺ ذكرت بعض نسائه كنيسة رأينها بأرض الحبشة يقال لها مارية وكانت أم سلمة وأم حبيبة رضى الله تعالى عنهما أتتا أرض الحبشة فذكرتا من حسنها وتصاوير فيها فرفع رأسه، فقال أولئك إذا مات منهم الرجل الصالح بنوا على قبره مسجدا ثم صوروا فيه تلك الصورة أولئك شرار الخلق عند الله
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was ill, some of his wives mentioned a church they had seen in the land of al-Habashah, called Mariyah. Umm Salamah and Umm Habibah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, had been to the land of al-Habashah. They mentioned its beauty and pictures in it. He raised his head and said, “Those people, when a righteous man among them dies, build a place of worship over his grave, then make that image in it. Those are the worst of creation before Allah.”

comparisons.note: Uses plural pictures where selected and modern have singular that image. The historical print does have a plural, so the comparison follows a documented alternate wording rather than an unsupported plural.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Aisha:

When the Prophet became ill, some of his wives talked about a church which they had seen in Ethiopia and it was called Mariya. Um Salma and Um Habiba had been to Ethiopia, and both of them narrated its (the Church's) beauty and the pictures it contained. The Prophet raised his head and said, "Those are the people who, whenever a pious man dies amongst them, make a place of worship at his grave and then they make those pictures in it. Those are the worst creatures in the Sight of Allah."
comparisons.note: Uses plural pictures where selected and modern have singular that image. The historical print does have a plural, so the comparison follows a documented alternate wording rather than an unsupported plural.

segments.arabic: [1277] حدثنا محمد بن سنان حدثنا فليح بن سليمان حدثنا هلال بن علي عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us: Hilal ibn ‘Ali related to us, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: شهدنا بنت رسول الله ﷺ ورسول الله ﷺ جالس على القبر فرأيت عينيه تدمعان، فقال هل فيكم من أحد لم يقارف الليلة، فقال أبو طلحة أنا قال: فانزل في قبرها فنزل في قبرها فقبرها
segments.english: We attended a daughter of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sitting by the grave, and I saw his eyes shedding tears. He asked, “Is there anyone among you who did not have intercourse last night?” Abu Talhah said, “I.” He said, “Then go down into her grave.” He went down into her grave and buried her.

segments.arabic: قال ابن مبارك قال: فليح أراه يعني الذنب
segments.english: Ibn Mubarak said: Fulayh said, “I think he means sin.”

segments.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله ليقترفوا أي ليكتسبوا
segments.english: Abu ‘Abd Allah said: “That they may acquire”—that is, “that they may earn.”

comparisons.note: Omits the Ibn Mubarak route. The intercourse rendering is a documented classical lexical choice, while Fulayh’s tentative sin gloss remains separately attributed; neither gloss is an explicit object in the selected question.

checkedBody: Narrated Anas:

We were in the funeral procession of the daughter of Allah's Apostle and Allah's Apostle was sitting near the grave and I saw his eyes full of tears. He said, "Is there anyone amongst you who did not have sexual relations with his wife last night?" Abu Talha replied in the affirmative. And so Allah's Apostle told him to get down in her grave and he got down in her grave and buried her.
comparisons.note: Adds with his wife and omits both Fulayh’s closing gloss and the Abu Abd Allah lexical note.

notes: The full selected closing contains Ibn Mubarak, Fulayh and Abu Abd Allah attributions. They need distinct roles, including the lexical note after the account.

segments.arabic: [1278] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف حدثنا الليث قال: حدثني ابن شهاب عن عبد الرحمن بن كعب بن مالك عن جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يجمع بين الرجلين من قتلى أحد في ثوب واحد ثم يقول أيهم أكثر أخذا للقرآن فإذا أشير له إلى أحدهما قدمه في اللحد، وقال: أنا شهيد على هؤلاء يوم القيامة وأمر بدفنهم في دمائهم ولم يغسلوا ولم يصل عليهم
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to bring together two of the men killed at Uhud in one garment. Then he would ask, “Which of them had learned more of the Qur’an?” When one of the two was pointed out to him, he placed him first in the side niche of the grave. He said, “I am a witness for these on the Day of Resurrection.” He ordered them to be buried in their blood. They were not washed, nor were they prayed over.

segments.arabic: [1279] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف حدثنا الليث حدثني يزيد بن أبي حبيب عن أبي الخير عن عقبة بن عامر

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ خرج يوما فصلى على أهل أحد صلاته على الميت ثم انصرف إلى المنبر، فقال إني فرط لكم وأنا شهيد عليكم وإني والله لأنظر إلى حوضي الآن وإني أعطيت مفاتيح خزائن الأرض أو مفاتيح الأرض وإني والله ما أخاف عليكم أن تشركوا بعدي ولكن أخاف عليكم أن تنافسوا فيها
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out one day and prayed over the people of Uhud as he prayed over the dead. Then he turned to the pulpit and said, “I am going ahead of you, and I am a witness over you. By Allah, I am looking at my basin now. I have been given the keys to the treasures of the earth—or the keys of the earth. By Allah, I do not fear that you will associate partners after me, but I fear that you will compete over it.”

comparisons.note: Renders تنافسوا as fighting; review the Arabic competition wording.

checkedBody: Narrated 'Uqba bin 'Amir:

One day the Prophet went out and offered the funeral prayers of the martyrs of Uhud and then went up the pulpit and said, "I will pave the way for you as your predecessor and will be a witness on you. By Allah! I see my Fount (Kauthar) just now and I have been given the keys of all the treasures of the earth (or the keys of the earth). By Allah! I am not afraid that you will worship others along with Allah after my death, but I am afraid that you will fight with one another for the worldly things."
comparisons.note: Adds the Kauthar identification and explanatory parentheses; the competition wording needs direct Arabic review.

checkedBody: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah :

Allah's Apostle shrouded every two martyrs of Uhud in one piece of cloth and then he would ask, "Which of them knew more Quran?" When one of them was pointed out he would put him first in the grave. segments.arabic: [1284] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله بن حوشب حدثنا عبد الوهاب حدثنا خالد عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hawshab related to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us: Khalid related to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: حرم الله مكة فلم تحل لأحد قبلي ولا لأحد بعدي أحلت لي ساعة من نهار لا يختلى خلاها ولا يعضد شجرها ولا ينفر صيدها ولا تلتقط لقطتها إلا لمعرف، فقال العباس رضى الله تعالى عنه إلا الإذخر لصاغتنا وقبورنا، فقال إلا الإذخر،
segments.english: “Allah made Makkah sacred. It was not made lawful for anyone before me or anyone after me. It was made lawful for me for a time during one day. Its fresh grass is not to be cut, its trees are not to be cut down, its game is not to be frightened away, and its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who makes it known.” Al-‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said, “Except idhkhir, for our goldsmiths and our graves.” He said, “Except idhkhir.”

segments.arabic: وقال أبو هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ لقبورنا وبيوتنا،
segments.english: And Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, said, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “For our graves and our houses.”

segments.arabic: وقال أبان بن صالح عن الحسن بن مسلم عن صفية بنت شيبة سمعت النبي ﷺ مثله،
segments.english: And Aban ibn Salih said, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah: I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say the same.

segments.arabic: وقال مجاهد عن طاوس عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما لقينهم وبيوتهم
segments.english: And Mujahid said, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, “For their smith and their houses.”

checkedBody: Narrated Ibn Abbas:

The Prophet said, "Allah has made Mecca a sanctuary (sacred place) and it was a sanctuary before me and will be so after me. It was made legal for me (to fight in it) for a few hours of the day. None is allowed to uproot its thorny shrubs or to cut its trees or to chase its game or to pick up its fallen things except by a person who announces it publicly." On that Al-Abbas said (to the Prophet), "Except Al-Idhkhir for our goldsmiths and for our graves." And so the Prophet added, "Except Al-Idhkhir. " And Abu Huraira narrated that the Prophet said, "Except Al-Idhkhir for our graves and houses." And Ibn Abbas said, "For their goldsmiths and houses."

segments.arabic: [1285] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله حدثنا سفيان قال عمرو سمعت جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us: Sufyan related to us. ‘Amr said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, say:

segments.arabic: أتى رسول الله ﷺ عبد الله بن أبي بعد ما أدخل حفرته فأمر به فأخرج فوضعه على ركبتيه ونفث عليه من ريقه وألبسه قميصه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy after he had been placed in his burial pit. He gave an order concerning him, and he was brought out. He placed him on his knees, blew lightly on him with some of his saliva and clothed him in his shirt.

segments.arabic: فالله أعلم
segments.english: Allah knows best.

segments.arabic: وكان كسا عباسا قميصا
segments.english: He had clothed ‘Abbas in a shirt.

segments.arabic: قال سفيان، وقال أبو هارون وكان على رسول الله ﷺ قميصان، فقال له بن عبد الله يا رسول الله ألبس أبي قميصك الذي يلي جلدك
segments.english: Sufyan said: And Abu Harun said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was wearing two shirts. The son of ‘Abd Allah said to him, “Messenger of Allah, clothe my father in the shirt of yours that is next to your skin.”

segments.arabic: قال سفيان فيرون أن النبي ﷺ ألبس عبد الله قميصه مكافأة لما صنع
segments.english: Sufyan said: They consider that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, clothed ‘Abd Allah in his shirt in return for what he had done.

comparisons.note: Names Abu Hurayra where selected and modern have Abu Harun, agreeing with the historical variant. Also joins the Allah-knows statement to the next report about the shirt, obscuring its boundary.

checkedBody: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah:

Allah's Apostle came to Abdullah bin Ubai (a hypocrite) after his death and he has been laid in his pit (grave). He ordered (that he be taken out of the grave) and he was taken out. Then he placed him on his knees and threw some of his saliva on him and clothed him in his (the Prophet's) own shirt. Allah knows better (why he did so). 'Abdullah bin Ubai had given his shirt to Al-Abbas to wear. Abu Harun said, "Allah's Apostle at that time had two shirts and the son of 'Abdullah bin Ubai said to him, 'O Allah's Apostle! Clothe my father in your shirt which has been in contact with your skin.' ' Sufyan added, "Thus people think that the Prophet clothed 'Abdullah bin Tubal in his shirt in lieu of what he (Abdullah) had done (for Al Abbas, the Prophet's uncle.)"
comparisons.note: Adds explanatory parentheses and corrupts the closing Ibn Ubayy name. Keep Sufyan, Abu Harun and the unnamed group’s inference separate.

segments.arabic: [1286] حدثنا مسدد أخبرنا بشر بن المفضل حدثنا حسين المعلم عن عطاء عن جابر رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal informed us: Husayn al-Mu‘allim related to us, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: لما حضر أحد دعاني أبي من الليل، فقال: ما أراني إلا مقتولا في أول من يقتل من أصحاب النبي ﷺ وإني لا أترك بعدي أعز علي منك غير نفس رسول الله ﷺ فإن علي دينا فاقض واستوص بأخواتك خيرا فأصبحنا فكان أول قتيل ودفن معه آخر في قبر ثم لم تطب نفسي أن أتركه مع الآخر فاستخرجته بعد ستة أشهر فإذا هو كيوم وضعته هنية غير أذنه
segments.english: When Uhud approached, my father called me during the night and said, “I expect to be killed among the first of the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to be killed. I leave no one behind dearer to me than you, except the person of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I have a debt, so pay it, and treat your sisters well.” When morning came, he was the first killed. Another was buried with him in a grave. Then I was not content to leave him with the other, so I took him out after six months. He was as he had been on the day I laid him there, except for a small change at his ear.

comparisons.note: Contains an asterisk in place of a complete honorific and abridges chains; the small-change/ear phrase needs careful lexical review.

checkedBody: Narrated Jabir:

When the time of the Battle of Uhud approached, my father called me at night and said, "I think that I will be the first amongst the companions of the Prophet to be martyred. I do not leave anyone after me dearer to me than you, except Allah's Apostle's soul and I owe some debt and you should repay it and treat your sisters favorably (nicely and politely)." So in the morning he was the first to be martyred and was buried along with another (martyr). I did not like to leave him with the other (martyr) so I took him out of the grave after six months of his burial and he was in the same condition as he was on the day of burial, except a slight change near his ear.
comparisons.note: Changes the father’s expectation of being among the first killed into being the first; the later narrator statement separately says he was first.

notes: The father’s expectation and the later report of what happened are distinct statements; do not flatten their different scope.

segments.arabic: [1288] حدثنا عبدان أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا الليث بن سعد قال: حدثني ابن شهاب عن عبد الرحمن بن كعب بن مالك عن جابر بن عبد الله رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdan related to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Al-Layth ibn Sa‘d informed us; he said: Ibn Shihab related to me, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يجمع بين رجلين من قتلى أحد ثم يقول أيهم أكثر أخذا للقرآن فإذا أشير له إلى أحدهما قدمه في اللحد، فقال: أنا شهيد على هؤلاء يوم القيامة فأمر بدفنهم بدمائهم ولم يغسلهم
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to bring together two men killed at Uhud. Then he would ask, “Which of them had learned more of the Qur’an?” When one of the two was pointed out to him, he placed him first in the side niche of the grave. He said, “I am a witness for these on the Day of Resurrection.” He ordered them to be buried in their blood, and he did not wash them.

comparisons.note: Adds a single-garment phrase absent from this occurrence and turns the final not-washing statement into an instruction.

checkedBody: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah:

The Prophet collected every two martyrs of Uhud (in one grave) and then he would ask, "Which of them knew the Quran more?" And if one of them was pointed out for him as having more knowledge, he would put him first in the Lahd. The Prophet said, "I will be a witness on these on the Day of Resurrection." Then he ordered them to be buried with their blood on their bodies and he did not have them washed.
comparisons.note: Supplies one grave; retain the complete chain and distinction between the burial order and the reported not-washing act.
